title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Virginia's 11th Congressional District
description: Virginia's 11th Congressional District, covering most of Fairfax County and the cities of Fairfax, Vienna, and Herndon, is holding its regularly scheduled general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democratic Rep. James Walkinshaw, who won a 2025 special election following the death of Rep. Gerry Connolly, is seeking a full term. He faces Republican nominee Arthur Purves, a retired computer programmer and longtime president of the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance. The district is considered a safe Democratic seat, and the race will test whether Republican messaging on federal spending and inflation can gain traction in this heavily blue Northern Virginia district.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the 2026 Virginia 11th Congressional District general election as of this writing. The district is rated as 'Solid Democratic' by most nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: James Walkinshaw
candidates.summary: James Walkinshaw is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 11th Congressional District, first elected in a September 2025 special election. He previously served on the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors representing the Braddock District from 2020 to 2025, and before that was Chief of Staff to the late Rep. Gerry Connolly for over a decade. In Congress, he serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform and Homeland Security Committees, and co-founded the Federal Workforce Caucus to defend the civil service. His campaign priorities include defending democracy, protecting federal workers, expanding affordable housing, combating climate change, and preserving reproductive rights.

candidates.name: Arthur Purves
candidates.summary: Arthur Purves is the Republican nominee for Virginia's 11th Congressional District. He is a retired computer programmer who has served as president of the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance for 29 years and has run for local offices seven times. His campaign focuses on reducing federal deficits by addressing chronic disease through food reform, opposing what he views as an overregulated food supply and energy policy, and cutting federal spending. Purves holds a BA, MS, and MBA from the University of Pennsylvania and has been active in Fairfax County civic and school advisory committees.
